  567.86 | &
  537.05 | Foreword
  516.48 | The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) is the sole apex
  507.78 | body responsibleforregulatingthe professionof Accountants and matters
  499.08 | connected therewith in Bangladesh. The education and qualification imparted by
  490.37 | the ICAB in Accountancy is recognized as the highest professional education and
  481.68 | qualification in the country. The members of the ICAB are known as Chartered
  472.97 | Accountants and they are allowed to use the designatory letters ACA or FCA as
  464.28 | granted by the Institute.
  451.58 | ICAB was established under the Bangladesh Chartered Accountants Order 1973
  442.88 | (P.O.No.2 of 1973). Institute initially started functioning with only 78 members
  434.18 | which has now grown to a membership size of 2034.ICAB has regional offices in
  425.48 | Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Rangpur, Khulna, Barishal, Sylhet and Mymensingh.
  416.77 | There are three overseas chapters of Dhaka Regional Committee i.e. one in
  408.07 | London and others in Toronto and Sydney.
  395.37 | ICAB is the primary regulator of Accounting & Auditing profession in the country
  386.67 | with mottos of ensuring transparency, accountability,integrityand good
  377.96 | governance in the financial sector of the economy of Bangladesh.
  365.26 | The responsibilities of the Institute are to conduct the professional examinations,
  356.56 | award membership of the Institute to qualified Chartered Accountants, issuance
  347.85 | of Practicing Certificates(CoP) to the members, maintain the status and standard
  339.15 | of professional qualifications and regulate the members of the Institute within the
  330.45 | purview of the Bangladesh Chartered Accountants Order 1973 and the Institute of
  321.74 | Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh Bye-laws,1973 (as amended up to 31
  313.04 | August 2023 and insertions thereafter). In addition, the Institute has to make
  304.33 | liaison with variousGovernment agencies,localand international Accounting
  295.63 | bodies and business houses. Ithas alsoto organize trainingcourses for its
  286.93 | members, students and other institutions to update and enrich their knowledge
  278.23 | on the profession of accountancy, auditing and information technology and legal
  269.53 | and statutory obligations and so on.
  256.83 | ICAB is a permanent member of several international and regional accounting
  248.12 | bodies includingthe IFAC (InternationalFederation of Accountants), IASB
  239.42 | (International Accounting Standards Board), CAPA (Confederation of Asian and
  230.72 | Pacific Accountants)and SAFA (South Asian Federation of Accountants). It
  222.02 | regularly participates in international and regional seminars and workshops across
  213.32 | the world. It also hosts such seminars and workshops in the country.
  200.62 | More than one-fourth of the Institute’s active membership is currently in public
  191.91 | practice, working inaccountancy firmsof all sizesfrom sole practitioners to
  183.21 | affiliates of large international firms and partnerships. The rest of the members are
  174.51 | employed in industry,financeand commerce and playing a wide variety of
  165.80 | financial, management and senior policymaking roles-both at home and abroad.
  153.10 | The Institute is governed by a Council comprising 20 members elected from the
  144.40 | two regional constituencies in Bangladesh headed by an elected President who is
  135.69 | the Chief Executive of the Council. The term of the council is for 3 years & period
  127.00 | of the presidency is for 1 year. The Council’s main responsibilities are the overall
  118.29 | management of the affairs and the business of the Institute including formulation,
  109.60 | setting and review of strategic policies. It provides advice and support to the
  100.90 | Government and various other stockholders when requested.
   88.20 | The day-to-day running of the Institute is delegated to the Secretariat, headed by
   79.49 | the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The Secretariat is located at CA Bhaban, 100
   70.79 | Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, Kawran Bazar, Dhaka-1215, Bangladesh. All
   62.08 | divisions/departments can be contacted on the phones: 880-9609612100,
   53.38 | 880-2-9115340, 9117521.
   41.59 | 05

  537.05 | Explanatory Notes
  508.31 | i. Members of the Institute are entitled to describe themselves as
  492.50 | Chartered Accountants.
  476.70 | ii. ACA denotes an Associate Member of the Institute.
  460.90 | iii. FCA denotes a Fellow Member of the Institute.
  445.09 | iv. The year in brackets, immediately after the name of a member,
  434.29 | denotes his/her year of admission into the Institute.
  418.49 | v. The date in bracket, after the designatory letters ACA/FCA, denotes
  407.69 | the
  391.88 | date he/she became an ACA/FCA
  376.08 | vi. The figure in bracket, at the end of the name of each member,
  365.28 | denoteshis/her enrolment number.
  318.31 | Key
  288.36 | * - indicate a member’s entitlement to train articled students
  274.56 | (Ph) - telephone
  260.76 | (O) - office telephone
  246.97 | (R) - residence telephone
  233.17 | (M) - mobile
  219.37 | (F) - fax
  205.57 | (E) - e-mail
  191.78 | (W) - website
